solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Transporter of love by cornet, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the three words might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A cornet player sends a love message by brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' tells you to rearrange LOVE BY CORNET, twelve letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving belt in a factory or airport carries goods along, so it is a kind of transporter.

clue.text: Opera firm's baby, dropping pole, almost complete

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm; with the 's it gives COS

indicators.note: dropping says a letter falls out of the word for baby

parts.note: an infant is a baby
N is the north pole

indicators.note: almost says the word for complete stops short of its final letter

parts.note: utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: A company's infant is nearly finished but has lost something polar along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping pole' takes N out of INFANT, leaving IFANT; 'almost' cuts the last letter from UTTER, giving UTTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's comic work about two sisters and their disguised lovers is a famous opera.

clue.text: Retreat back with some lucky numbers: his followers had a smashing time.

definitions.text: his followers had a smashing time

indicators.note: back tells you the word for retreat is read from right to left

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: some says only part of the word lucky is used, its opening pair of letters with the rest dropped

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, so two of them make two numbers

explanation.surface: A punter retreats home with lucky numbers, while some followers enjoy a riotous party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the retreat word and 'some' trims lucky. The Luddites, early 19th-century English textile workers, smashed machines in the name of the mythical Ned Ludd.
explanation.definitionFit: The machine-breaking Luddites took their name from this legendary leader, so his followers literally smashed things.

clue.text: Vermicidal satellite

definitions.meaning: worm-killing: the proverb says this early riser catches the worm
the name of the first commercial communications satellite, launched in 1965

explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial early riser catches and kills the worm, and Intelsat I bore the same nickname.

clue.text: Prize for stretch limo, perhaps

parts.note: a stretched vehicle is outsize, abbreviated OS as in clothing sizes
a limousine is one example of a car

explanation.surface: A film award goes to a long luxury car.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes limousines at the Academy Awards ceremony; 'stretch' is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette is the film world's best-known prize.

clue.text: Clip for a friend

definitions.meaning: a strong spring clip for holding papers
a dog is called man's best friend, and this stocky breed is one

explanation.definitionFit: A spring-loaded paper clamp shares its name with a sturdy dog breed, a loyal canine companion.

clue.text: Drop left out completely

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of left are rearranged

parts.note: all means completely, as in all gone

explanation.surface: An item dropped was left out entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow something to slip from your hand is to drop it.

clue.text: Splitter on October 1st, curved or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

parts.note: first is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Something divides on the first of October, whether curved or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' mixes OCT, I and CURVED OR into the answer's twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A court where marriages are dissolved splits couples apart, so it is jokingly a splitter.

clue.text: Wrong sort of trading in liquor, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the liquor is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Dealing in alcohol is a dubious sort of business.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDER is the spelling that sounds like CIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading on confidential company knowledge is illegal, the classic wrong sort of dealing, and is named after the person with that knowledge.

clue.text: Small house available without lease for French novelist

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for small house wraps around another

parts.note: a cote is a small shelter, as in dovecote
to let is to lease out property

explanation.surface: A cottage on the market without a tenancy agreement suits a writer from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside. 'available' only supports the property picture, since houses offered to let are available.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidonie-Gabrielle, author of Gigi and the Claudine novels, was a celebrated writer from France.

clue.text: Always those fish point to the rest of the world

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
yon is an old or dialect word for that or those over there
an eel is a long snake-like fish
SE is the compass point south-east

explanation.surface: Fishermen always point their catch at the wider world.
explanation.definitionFit: All other people besides oneself make up the rest of the world.

clue.text: At leisure and no longer available for tax

definitions.meaning: read as goods taken off the list of items that carry a customs charge

explanation.definitionFit: A worker on time off is free, and goods with the levy removed are literally free of the charge.

clue.text: Spread out at speed and help to get back in

indicators.note: in places the turned word for help inside the word for speed

parts.note: rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

indicators.note: to get back says the word for help is reversed

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone spreads out fast and then help returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get back' turns AID into DIA, which goes 'in' RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat or light that radiates spreads outward from a centre.

clue.text: Is it possible for journalist to be given the stick?

parts.note: can asks whether something is possible
ED, short for editor, is a crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter wonders whether being beaten is on the cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten with a rod is being punished with a stick.

clue.text: Unhealthy (say) friend breaking the rules

parts.note: ill means unwell
eg, for example, is what say means when it introduces an instance
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A sickly companion is flouting regulations.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting against the law is the adverbial sense of flouting regulations.

clue.text: Military exploit delaying All Fools' Day?

definitions.meaning: Mao's 1934-35 retreat of the Red Army across China
if the third month lasted longer, the first of April would be put off

explanation.definitionFit: The epic 1934 Chinese Communist retreat is famous as a military feat, and an extended month would push back April Fool's Day.

clue.text: Lend coach out to council town, an endless gem

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A coach is lent out to a town council, along with a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LEND COACH. 'an endless gem' is a second hint: chalcedony, a quartz gemstone, with its last letter cut.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient town in Asia Minor hosted the Church Council of 451.

clue.text: Officer doing 500 miles in sea

indicators.note: in tells you the number and distance sit inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia
D is the Roman numeral 500
MI is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A naval officer covers five hundred miles at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest-ranking naval commander is a senior officer.

clue.text: Wine is less than tea and less than happiness

indicators.note: less than suggests the word for tea is cut short by a letter

parts.note: char is British slang for tea

indicators.note: the second less than shortens the word for happiness by its last letter

parts.note: bliss is great happiness

explanation.surface: A drinker ranks wine below both tea and contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR loses R to give CHA; BLISS loses an S to give BLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The dry white from Burgundy's northernmost district is a well-known wine.

clue.text: Dresser in two generations

parts.note: ma, a mother, is one generation
a son is the generation after his mother

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture handed down through a mother and son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresser' suggests furniture, but here it is someone who dresses stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason dresses, or shapes, blocks of stone, so he is a stone dresser.

clue.text: Country with a large number of stale eggs

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
old means stale, past its best
ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A nation stocks a huge quantity of past-it eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlocked state between Romania and Ukraine is a country of eastern Europe.

clue.text: Scottish water beast with local expression

parts.note: a seal is a marine animal
och is a Scottish exclamation, a local expression north of the border

explanation.surface: A creature in a Scottish lake utters a regional exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an arm of the sea reaching inland is a body of water with this name.

clue.text: Accidental encounter of a French setter and an insect

parts.note: un is French for a
me is the crossword compiler speaking of themselves
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A chance meeting between a Frenchman, a dog and a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests a dog, but it is the compiler, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done without intention is accidental.

clue.text: See 1
Benefit of distance and time

parts.note: a mile is a distance
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: The advantage of travelling far for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: To get mileage out of something is to obtain advantage or use from it.

clue.text: Model for painting permitted a single pastry

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
painting is a form of art
let means permitted

explanation.surface: An artist's model was allowed one cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model for painting' suggests an artist's sitter, but it splits into Model T and ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A small individual tart is a pastry made for one person.

clue.text: Disorderly Olympic destination to the British

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympic Games
us, from a British setter's point of view, means the British

explanation.surface: Unruly fans head off to the Olympic city, leaving Britain behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild, unruly and lawless behaviour is disorderly.

clue.text: Scene of witches initiating Berners Lee as premier

indicators.note: initiating means taking the first letter of each of the two names

parts.note: Edward Heath was UK prime minister 1970-74, known as Ted

explanation.surface: The web's inventor stands in as prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web. The witches in Macbeth meet on a bleak heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare sets the witches' meeting with Macbeth on a wild windswept moor.
